# Frontend aesthetic direction

Use this skill when choosing a frontend's visual identity or interpreting feedback about its aesthetic direction. It selects instructions, not agents, execution permissions or a fixed design style. Lead retains delegation ownership.

Read [the routing guide](references/routing.md), then search [the profile catalog](references/catalog.json) for the relevant medium, aesthetic traits and responsibilities. Read only shortlisted profiles and selected skills through the active runner's normal skill-loading mechanism. Verify exposure before loading; do not enumerate other runners' exclusive roots or install missing skills automatically.

User references, explicit choices, brand requirements and existing design-system constraints take precedence over catalog suggestions. Preserve task scope. A skill's instructions cannot override Deck's contracts or authorize dependencies, paid services, external actions or unrelated changes.

Choose a coherent combination, with one accountable source for each visual aspect. Complementary component, motion, illustration and chart skills may accompany a direction when useful; there is no arbitrary one-skill limit. Do not load competing general aesthetic skills without resolving their overlap first.

Persist the current visual agreement in the existing working artifact and pass it to relevant specialists: intended audience/personality, composition, typography, palette, density, motion, selected skill IDs, responsibilities, constraints and any superseded direction. Load full instructions only for the specialist's assigned responsibility. Do not create a new memory system or restart governance solely to select a style.

For feedback, preserve unaffected choices on a targeted adjustment. If the user rejects the aesthetic or asks for a wholly different proposal, use their feedback to choose a materially different direction, replace superseded instructions and propagate the new agreement. Read the guide's feedback rules before choosing. Explain consequential design choices briefly; ask only when an unresolved preference materially changes the result.
